# Code Review — 2026-08-17

## Scope
- Repo: `danieljustus/symaira-appkit` (SPM Swift library, macOS 14+/iOS 17+, Swift 6 strict concurrency, zero third-party deps)
- HEAD: `140b838` (main, clean). Cycle since the last review (`2c8d2c1`, 2026-08-12): #80–#85 plus the 0.10.0 release — Keychain user-presence access control (#82), `UpdateApplier` split into `AssetDownloader`/`AppInstaller`/`ChecksumManifest`/`InstallMethod` with streaming downloads (#83), MCPTypes and auto-update coverage (#80, #81).
- Prior findings re-verified: redaction gaps **fixed** (`CLIRunner.swift:123-139` now carries provider-prefixed patterns), Keychain access control **fixed** (`SymairaKeychain.swift:69-105`), in-memory download **fixed** (`AssetDownloader.swift:169-238` streams and caps before the body is read), `UpdateApplier` size **fixed** (1163 → 345 lines), README `SymairaMCP` row **fixed**. None re-flagged.
- Evidence base: full read-through of `Sources/` (8 modules, ~6.5k LOC), CI/CodeQL/Dependabot workflows, `Package.swift`, README/AGENTS/DESIGN, coverage report 2026-08-12 (87.4%), and the cosign/update-apply test fixtures.

## Findings

- [ ] **[Security] Cosign verification signs a re-serialized dictionary, so it can never validate a real `checksums.txt`**
  - **Status quo:** `Sources/SymairaUpdateCheck/UpdateApplier.swift:187` hands `CosignVerification.verify` the *parsed* `[String: String]` map, and `Sources/SymairaUpdateCheck/Cosign.swift:249-256` rebuilds the signed content by iterating that dictionary (`for (name, sum) in checksums`). Swift dictionary order is unspecified and per-process seeded, so any manifest with two or more entries produces different bytes than the file goreleaser actually signed — `cosign verify-blob` fails. Original formatting (comments, blank lines, `*` binary markers, CRLF) is lost too. The tag is also re-prefixed unconditionally as `.../v\(v)/...` at `Cosign.swift:164`, while the ecosystem's documented tag scheme is unprefixed (`AGENTS.md:32`) — a second 404 path. Separately, `apply(release:)` (`UpdateApplier.swift:114-144`) performs no cosign step at all, so the raw-binary update path silently skips signature verification even when `cosignConfig` is set. The existing tests (`Tests/SymairaUpdateCheckTests/UpdateApplierTests.swift:832+`) use stub verifiers, so none of this is caught.
  - **Proposed solution:** Keep the raw checksums body from `fetchChecksums` and pass those exact bytes to `CosignVerification.verify` instead of the parsed map (return `(Data, [String: String])`). Make the artifact URL tag-scheme-agnostic: try the release's `tagName` verbatim first, fall back to the `v`-prefixed form. Move the cosign step into a shared private helper called by both `apply(release:)` and `applyBundle(release:)`. Add a test asserting the bytes handed to the verifier equal the downloaded body verbatim for a multi-entry manifest.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Security] Default cosign identity regexp is never applied — `--certificate-identity-regexp ""` accepts any signer**
  - **Status quo:** `Sources/SymairaUpdateCheck/Cosign.swift:54-59` builds the default `CosignCLIVerifier` with the *raw* `identityRegexp`, which defaults to `""`. `CosignCLIVerifier.verifySignature` then passes that empty string straight to cosign at `Cosign.swift:223`. An empty identity regexp matches every certificate identity, so any Fulcio-issued signature from any GitHub Actions workflow passes verification. `identityRegexpOrDefault()` (`Cosign.swift:63-66`) exists precisely to avoid this but is only ever called from tests (`Tests/SymairaUpdateCheckTests/UpdateApplierTests.swift:804, 815`); the production path never reaches it — and `UpdateApplierTests.swift:826` pins `identityRegexp == ""` as the expected default.
  - **Proposed solution:** Have `CosignCLIVerifier` resolve the default itself (a private `identityRegexpOrDefault()` mirroring `CosignConfig`'s, used at the `--certificate-identity-regexp` call site), and hard-fail with `cosignVerificationFailed` if the resolved pattern is still empty. Add a test that captures the argv passed to the runner and asserts the identity flag is non-empty and repo-scoped.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Security] `BinaryLocator` documents rejecting unverified binaries but only gates on directory ownership**
  - **Status quo:** `Sources/SymairaToolKit/BinaryLocator.swift:18-24` states that binaries are "rejected if the containing directory is not root-owned…" and that every binary "is checked for a valid code signature… Pass `allowUnverified: true` to skip these checks." In `locate(_:allowUnverified:)` (`BinaryLocator.swift:78-128`) the flag only guards `isDirectorySecure`; `Self.verifySignature(at:)` results are recorded in `Located.verified` but never cause a rejection on any of the five branches. With the default `ToolDetector(allowUnverified: false)` (`Sources/SymairaToolKit/ToolDetector.swift:76`), an unsigned or tampered binary in `/opt/homebrew/bin` is still returned and then executed by `queryVersion` (`ToolDetector.swift:167-187`). Consumers reading the docstring will assume a guarantee that is not enforced.
  - **Proposed solution:** Either enforce it — skip candidates from `.path`/`.extraDirectory` when `verifySignature` fails and `allowUnverified` is false, keeping `.userOverride`/`.bundle` advisory as documented — or, if the permissive behavior is deliberate for Homebrew-installed cores that ship ad-hoc signatures, correct the docstring to say verification is advisory and surface `verified` in the detector so apps can gate execution themselves. Pick one and cover it with a test.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[UX/DX] Cosign lookup inherits the GUI PATH, so an installed cosign reports "not found"**
  - **Status quo:** `Sources/SymairaUpdateCheck/Cosign.swift:189-198` probes with `/usr/bin/which cosign` and then runs `/usr/bin/env cosign …` (`Cosign.swift:218`), both relying on the inherited `PATH`. `SubprocessRunner.run` never sets `process.environment` (`Sources/SymairaUpdateCheck/SubprocessRunner.swift:56-63`), so a GUI app launched from Finder gets `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` and the Homebrew-installed `cosign` is invisible. The user sees "cosign CLI not found — install cosign…" while cosign *is* installed. This is exactly the class already solved elsewhere in this repo (`CLIRunner.augmentedPATHPrefix`, `CLIRunner.swift:199-208`; `BinaryLocator`'s explicit Homebrew prefixes) but never applied to `SubprocessRunner`.
  - **Proposed solution:** Add an `environment:` parameter to `SubprocessRunner.run/runChecked` defaulting to `CLIRunner.augmentedEnvironment(ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment)` — or resolve cosign through `BinaryLocator` and invoke the absolute path instead of `/usr/bin/env`. Extend the error message with the searched prefixes so a real miss is diagnosable.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[UX/DX] README module table understates what `SymairaUpdateCheck` and `SymairaKeychain` now ship**
  - **Status quo:** `README.md:28-29` still describes `SymairaKeychain` as "Keychain wrapper, service-namespaced `dev.symaira.<app>`" and `SymairaUpdateCheck` as a "GitHub latest-release checker with disk cache and stable-semver comparison". Since 0.10.0 the former also offers the user-presence access control added in #82 (`SymairaKeychain.swift:69-105`) and automatic legacy-item migration; the latter now covers streaming asset download with a 1 GiB cap, SHA256 manifest verification, optional cosign verification, DMG/ZIP installation to `/Applications`, and Homebrew install-method rejection (`UpdateApplier.swift:27-102`). Consumers pinning 0.10.0 cannot discover any of it from the README.
  - **Proposed solution:** Extend the two table rows to name the shipped capabilities (one line each, matching the existing style) and add a short "Update flow" snippet under Usage showing `UpdateApplier(checkInstallMethod:cosignConfig:)` → `applyBundle(release:targetPath:)`.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[Architecture] `DaemonSupervisor.generation` is read and written outside the lock**
  - **Status quo:** `Sources/SymairaDaemonKit/DaemonSupervisor.swift:89-90` does `generation += 1` and reads it with no lock held, while `DaemonSupervisor.swift:151` reads it under `lock` in the termination handler and `DaemonSupervisor.swift:229, 236` read it unlocked from two `DispatchQueue.global` escalation blocks. The class is `@unchecked Sendable` (`:30`), so the compiler cannot catch this — it is a genuine data race on the very field whose job is to distinguish stale generations, and it is reachable by calling `start()` while a previous stop escalation is still pending. `stopInternal` reads it correctly under lock (`:201`), which makes the unguarded sites look accidental rather than deliberate.
  - **Proposed solution:** Move the increment and both escalation-block reads inside `lock` (a small `private func currentGeneration() -> UInt64` and `private func nextGeneration() -> UInt64` keeps call sites readable), or convert the whole supervisor to an `actor` and expose the callbacks as an `AsyncStream`. Add a test that calls `start()` twice in quick succession and asserts the first generation's escalation does not kill the second process.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Architecture] `MCPServer`'s built-in handlers retain `self`, so no server instance is ever deallocated**
  - **Status quo:** `Sources/SymairaMCP/MCPServer.swift:84-93` registers the `ping` and `initialize` handlers from within `init`, and the `initialize` closure captures `self` strongly (`self.protocolVersion`, `self.effectiveCapabilities`, `self.name`, `self.version`). Those closures are stored in `self.handlers` (`MCPServer.swift:140`) — a textbook retain cycle in a `final class`. Every `MCPServer` leaks along with its transport and handler table; a host app that constructs one server per connection or restarts a server on reconnect accumulates them. Relatedly, `write(_:)` reads `self.transport` without taking `lock` (`MCPServer.swift:292`) while `beginStart`/`stop` mutate it under the lock.
  - **Proposed solution:** Capture the needed values (`name`, `version`, `protocolVersion`) as locals before the closure and use `[weak self]` for the `effectiveCapabilities` lookup, returning empty capabilities when `self` is gone — or move built-in registration out of `init` into a `private func installBuiltins()` called from a static factory. Read `transport` through the existing locked accessor in `write(_:)`. A `weak var` reference test after dropping the strong one pins the fix.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[Performance] Streaming downloads iterate `URLSession.AsyncBytes` one byte at a time**
  - **Status quo:** `Sources/SymairaUpdateCheck/AssetDownloader.swift:52-59` builds each 64 KiB chunk with `while chunk.count < chunkSize, let byte = try await inner.next() { chunk.append(byte) }` — one async suspension point and one `Data.append` per byte. That is ~65,536 awaits per chunk and roughly 500 million for a 500 MB DMG; `AsyncBytes` byte-wise iteration is the well-known slow path and typically caps throughput far below the network link, turning app updates into multi-minute operations even on fast connections. The size cap the same commit introduced is correct and worth keeping; only the chunking mechanism is the bottleneck.
  - **Proposed solution:** Replace `URLSession.AsyncBytes` with a `URLSessionDataDelegate`/`URLSessionDownloadDelegate` that yields whole `Data` chunks into an `AsyncStream` (the `UpdateByteStream` seam already in place absorbs the change with no call-site edits), or at minimum drain via `inner.chunks(ofCount:)`-style batching. Keep the `Content-Length` pre-check, the running-count abort, and the per-chunk `SHA256`/progress behavior exactly as they are; existing `AssetDownloaderTests` cover them.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[Performance] `async` update paths block cooperative-pool threads on synchronous subprocess waits**
  - **Status quo:** `CosignCLIVerifier.verifySignature` is `async` (`Sources/SymairaUpdateCheck/Cosign.swift:187`) but calls the fully blocking `SubprocessRunner.runChecked` twice (`Cosign.swift:189, 217`), which parks the calling thread on a `DispatchSemaphore` for up to 30s plus a 3s grace and a further 3s after SIGKILL (`SubprocessRunner.swift:128-151`). The same pattern runs from `applyBundle`, an `async` function, through `AppInstaller.installDMG`/`installZip` (`UpdateApplier.swift:215-217`), which shell out to `hdiutil`, `ditto`, and `xattr` (`AppInstaller.swift:63, 89, 138, 172`). Swift's cooperative pool has one thread per core; a 4-core Mac running two concurrent update flows can stall unrelated `async` work in the host app, including UI-driving tasks.
  - **Proposed solution:** Wrap the blocking calls so they never occupy a cooperative thread — either give `SubprocessRunner` an `async` variant built on `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` over a dedicated `DispatchQueue` (mirroring `CLIRunner.execute`), or hop the existing sync calls onto a detached executor. `CLIRunner` already demonstrates the non-blocking shape inside this repo.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / medium impact

## Conclusion

The last cycle's work landed cleanly — redaction, Keychain access control, the `UpdateApplier` split and streaming downloads all verified fixed, and coverage held at 87.4%. What this cycle surfaces is that the cosign hardening path, while structurally present, cannot succeed as shipped: the signed content is rebuilt from an unordered dictionary, and the identity regexp reaches cosign empty. Both are small, well-localized edits.

**Best first quick win:** apply the default identity regexp inside `CosignCLIVerifier` (`Sources/SymairaUpdateCheck/Cosign.swift:54-59, 223`) — a two-line change that closes an "accepts any signer" hole, with the correct default already written and tested one type away.
